description: Haemul Pajeon is a beloved Korean savory pancake, celebrated for its crispy edges and tender interior, generously studded with an array of fresh seafood and vibrant green onions. This culinary delight offers a harmonious blend of textures and umami flavors, making it a perfect appetizer or light meal. Enjoy a taste of Korea with every delicious bite of this traditional favorite.

ingredients.notes: shrimp, squid, mussels, clams, pre-cleaned and bite-sized

instructions.title: Prepare the Seafood and Vegetables
instructions.text: Thoroughly clean and pat dry the mixed seafood. If using larger pieces, cut them into bite-sized portions. Prepare the green onions by washing and trimming them, then cut them into 3-4 inch lengths. Thinly slice the onion and red chili if using. Set aside.

instructions.title: Make the Pancake Batter
instructions.text: In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, rice flour, and cold water until just combined. A few lumps are fine. Beat the egg separately and then gently fold it into the batter. Do not overmix the batter; it should be loose enough to spread.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dipping Sauce
instructions.text: In a small bowl, combine the soy sauce, rice vinegar, gochugaru (if using), sesame oil, and toasted sesame seeds. Stir well. You can also add a finely chopped green onion for extra flavor. Set aside.

instructions.title: Assemble the Pancake
instructions.text: Heat a large non-stick skillet or griddle over medium-high heat. Add about 2 tablespoons of cooking oil and swirl to coat the pan. Arrange a layer of green onion pieces in the hot oil, then scatter a portion of the sliced onion and mixed seafood over the green onions.

instructions.title: Cook the First Side of the Pancake
instructions.text: Pour about 1/2 to 3/4 cup of the batter over the seafood and vegetables, spreading it evenly to cover the ingredients and form a round pancake. You can press down lightly with a spatula to ensure everything is submerged. Cook for 5-7 minutes until the bottom is golden brown and crispy.

instructions.title: Flip and Finish Cooking
instructions.text: Carefully flip the pancake using a large spatula. Add another tablespoon of oil around the edges if needed to ensure crispiness. Cook for another 5-7 minutes until the second side is also golden brown and the seafood is fully cooked. If desired, crack another egg directly onto the cooked side and spread it lightly before flipping for an extra rich pancake.

instructions.title: Repeat and Serve
instructions.text: Slide the cooked Haemul Pajeon onto a cutting board. Cut into wedges immediately. Repeat the process with the remaining ingredients, adding more oil as needed for each pancake. Serve the hot Haemul Pajeon with the prepared dipping sauce.

tips: For the crispiest Pajeon, ensure your batter is made with cold water and dont overmix it. A slightly lumpy batter is ideal.
Dont overcrowd your pan. Cook one pancake at a time to ensure even cooking and a perfectly crispy texture.
Serve Haemul Pajeon immediately after cooking with the dipping sauce. It's best enjoyed hot for maximum crispiness and flavor.
article:
Discover the culinary delight that is Haemul Pajeon, a beloved Korean seafood pancake that tantalizes taste buds with its crispy edges, soft interior, and generous medley of fresh seafood and vibrant green onions. This savory sensation is more than just a dish; it's a culinary experience, perfect for sharing with friends and family, often accompanied by a refreshing glass of makgeolli (Korean rice wine). Whether you’ve encountered it in a bustling Seoul street market or a cozy Korean restaurant, the allure of Haemul Pajeon is undeniable. Now, imagine bringing that authentic taste right into your kitchen. This comprehensive guide will walk you through everything you need to know to master this iconic Korean dish.

## What is Haemul Pajeon (Korean Seafood Pancake)?

Haemul Pajeon, pronounced "Hae-mul Pah-jeon," translates literally to "seafood scallion pancake." It's a type of "jeon," a broad category of Korean pan-fried dishes made from various ingredients coated in a flour and egg batter. What sets Haemul Pajeon apart is its signature combination of fresh seafood (haemul) and an abundance of green onions (pa).

The magic of this pancake lies in its textural contrast. A perfectly cooked Haemul Pajeon boasts a beautifully golden-brown, crispy exterior that gives way to a tender, flavorful interior packed with succulent shrimp, chewy squid, and sometimes mussels or oysters. The long strands of green onion provide a mild, slightly sweet bite that complements the savory seafood and the light, airy batter. It’s a versatile dish, often served as an appetizer, a side dish (banchan), or even a light main course, especially popular on rainy days when its warm, comforting appeal is most sought after. Its rich history and widespread popularity make it a staple in Korean cuisine, cherished for its simplicity and incredible taste.

## Ingredients You Need for Haemul Pajeon

Crafting the perfect Haemul Pajeon requires a blend of fresh ingredients and a few pantry staples. Here’s what you’ll need to gather:

For the Pancake Batter:
*   1 cup all-purpose flour
*   1/4 cup glutinous rice flour (or cornstarch for extra crispiness)
*   1/2 teaspoon salt
*   1/4 teaspoon white pepper
*   1 1/2 cups ice-cold water (the colder, the crispier!)
*   1 large egg, lightly beaten

For the Seafood and Vegetables:
*   1/2 lb mixed seafood (e.g., shrimp, squid rings, mussels, baby octopus), cleaned and patted dry. Cut larger pieces into bite-sized portions.
*   8-10 large green onions (scallions), trimmed and cut into 3-4 inch lengths. You’ll want a generous amount.
*   1/2 small onion, thinly sliced
*   1 red chili pepper, thinly sliced (optional, for color and a touch of heat)
*   Vegetable oil, for frying

For the Dipping Sauce:
*   3 tablespoons soy sauce
*   1 tablespoon rice vinegar
*   1 teaspoon sesame oil
*   1 teaspoon toasted sesame seeds
*   1 clove garlic, minced
*   1/2 teaspoon gochugaru (Korean chili flakes, optional)

## Step-by-Step Instructions to Make Haemul Pajeon

Follow these steps to create your own delicious Haemul Pajeon at home:

1.  **Prepare the Seafood and Vegetables:** Ensure all your seafood is thoroughly cleaned, deveined (if shrimp), and patted completely dry with paper towels. Cut any larger pieces into bite-sized chunks. Slice the green onions into uniform 3-4 inch pieces. Thinly slice the onion and red chili (if using).
2.  **Make the Batter:** In a large bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, glutinous rice flour (or cornstarch), salt, and white pepper. Gradually add the ice-cold water and the beaten egg, whisking until just combined. A few lumps are okay; do not overmix, as this can lead to a tough pancake. The batter should be thin, like a crepe batter.
3.  **Prepare the Dipping Sauce:** In a small bowl, combine all the dipping sauce ingredients: soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, sesame seeds, minced garlic, and gochugaru (if using). Stir well and set aside.
4.  **Assemble and Cook the Pancake:** Heat 2-3 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a large non-stick skillet or cast-iron pan over medium-high heat. The pan should be hot enough that a drop of water sizzles instantly.
5.  **First Layer:** Pour about 1/2 cup of batter into the hot pan, spreading it thinly to form a round base. Quickly arrange a generous layer of green onion pieces over the batter, ensuring they are evenly distributed.
6.  **Add Seafood and More Batter:** Scatter a portion of the prepared seafood, sliced onion, and red chili (if using) evenly over the green onions. Drizzle another 1/4 cup of batter over the seafood and vegetables to bind everything together.
7.  **Cook and Flip:** Cook for 4-5 minutes on the first side, until the edges are golden brown and crispy, and the batter is mostly set. Using a large spatula (or two), carefully flip the Haemul Pajeon. Press down gently to ensure even cooking. Add another tablespoon of oil around the edges if needed to promote crispiness.
8.  **Second Side:** Cook for another 3-4 minutes, or until the second side is golden brown and the seafood is cooked through.
9.  **Serve:** Transfer the cooked Haemul Pajeon to a cutting board. Slice into wedges or squares and serve immediately with the prepared dipping sauce. Repeat the process for any remaining batter and ingredients.

## Pro Tips for the Best Crispy Haemul Pajeon

Achieving that perfect balance of crispy exterior and tender interior for your Haemul Pajeon isn't hard with a few expert tricks:

*   **Ice-Cold Water is Key:** Using ice water or very cold water in your batter helps to inhibit gluten development, resulting in a lighter, crisper pancake.
*   **Don't Overmix the Batter:** A few lumps are perfectly fine. Overmixing develops gluten, making the pancake tough and chewy rather than tender and crispy.
*   **Use a Mix of Flours:** While all-purpose flour forms the base, adding glutinous rice flour or cornstarch significantly enhances the crispiness of the pancake.
*   **Plenty of Oil:** Don't be shy with the oil. Haemul Pajeon is pan-fried, and enough oil is crucial for achieving that beautiful golden-brown, crispy crust. You might need to add a little more around the edges during cooking.
*   **Hot Pan, Then Moderate Heat:** Start with a hot pan to get that initial sizzle and crisp, then reduce the heat slightly to medium-high to ensure the ingredients cook through without burning the exterior.
*   **Thin Batter Layer:** While loaded with ingredients, the batter itself should be relatively thin to allow the green onions and seafood to shine and crisp up.
*   **Pat Seafood Dry:** Excess moisture from the seafood can make your pancake soggy. Always pat your shrimp, squid, and other seafood completely dry before adding them to the batter.

## Serving Suggestions for Your Seafood Pancake

Haemul Pajeon is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in many ways:

*   **Hot and Fresh:** Always serve your Haemul Pajeon immediately after cooking. Its crispy texture is best enjoyed straight from the pan.
*   **With Dipping Sauce:** The accompanying soy-vinegar dipping sauce is non-negotiable. Its tangy, savory, and slightly spicy notes perfectly cut through the richness of the pancake.
*   **As an Appetizer:** Cut into smaller squares or wedges, Haemul Pajeon makes an excellent starter for any Korean meal.
*   **As a Side Dish (Banchan):** Serve alongside other traditional Korean banchan like kimchi, pickled radishes, and seasoned spinach for a complete dining experience.
*   **Light Main Course:** For a lighter meal, a larger Haemul Pajeon can be enjoyed as the main dish, perhaps with a side of rice.
*   **Beverage Pairings:** Traditionally, Haemul Pajeon is famously paired with makgeolli (Korean rice wine), especially on rainy days. It also goes wonderfully with soju or a cold beer.

## Variations and Substitutions for Haemul Pajeon

While the classic Haemul Pajeon is fantastic, don't hesitate to experiment with variations to suit your taste or what you have on hand:

*   **Vegetarian Pajeon:** For a meat-free option, simply omit the seafood. Instead, load up on various vegetables like sliced mushrooms (shiitake, oyster), zucchini, bell peppers, carrots, or even kimchi.
*   **Kimchi Pajeon:** A popular variation, Kimchi Pajeon involves adding chopped kimchi to the batter for a spicy, tangy kick. You can still include seafood or add thinly sliced pork for a more robust flavor.
*   **Different Seafood Combinations:** Feel free to customize the seafood mix. Oysters, clams, or baby octopus are all excellent additions. Just ensure they are fresh and properly prepared.
*   **Add More Vegetables:** Beyond green onions, consider adding thinly sliced carrots, julienned zucchini, or a handful of bean sprouts for extra texture and nutrition.
*   **Spice It Up:** If you love heat, increase the amount of gochugaru in your dipping sauce or even add a pinch directly into the pancake batter.
*   **Gluten-Free Option:** For those with gluten sensitivities, substitute the all-purpose flour with a good quality gluten-free flour blend. You might need to adjust the water slightly to achieve the right batter consistency.

Making Haemul Pajeon at home is a rewarding experience that brings a taste of authentic Korean cuisine to your table. With its delightful combination of crispy texture, fresh seafood, and savory flavors, this seafood pancake is sure to become a favorite. So, gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to impress your taste buds with this iconic Korean dish. Enjoy the process, savor the flavors, and share the joy of homemade Haemul Pajeon!
